samples.summary: assoc-1 selection mapping only fixes the pure-insertion case; a caret at column 0 of a line whose prefix is *replaced* still ends up in front of the new marker
samples.evidence: `view.state.selection.map(changeSet, 1)` changes behaviour only for zero-length changes. `ChangeDesc.mapPos` returns `pos == posA || assoc < 0 ? posB : posB + ins`, i.e. when the position sits exactly at the START of a replaced range (len > 0) it maps to the range start regardless of assoc. Concretely: doc `"- a"`, caret 0, click the Task toggle -> replacePrefixes emits {from:0, to:2, insert:'- [ ] '}; mapPos(0, 1) hits `endA(2) > pos(0)` and returns posB = 0, so the caret stays at column 0 in front of `- [ ] a`. The next keystroke produces `x- [ ] a` — exactly the corruption the new comment (lines 208-211) claims to have fixed. Same for ordered->bullet, bullet->ordered and indent/outdent via `shift()`, where the prefix is always a replacement rather than an insertion. Only the blank-line/plain-line case (from == to, the new test at list-commands.test.ts:40) is actually repaired.

samples.summary: Only `summary` was exempted: clicking the body of a `<details>` nested in a task item still rewrites the task's source line
samples.evidence: The guard is `if (target.closest('a, button, summary')) return;`. For the very markup the new test renders (`- [ ] todo` + an indented `<details>` block, preview.test.ts:197-199) the whole disclosure — `details`, its body paragraphs, fences, etc. — lives inside `li.task-list-item`. A click on the folded body text passes `clickedItem = target.closest('li') === item`, so line 315-317 flip the task's checkbox and sync a source edit, which is the same defect the summary exemption was added to avoid ("toggling would edit a line nobody pointed at"). A click on the `<details>` element's own padding area outside the summary has the same effect. The exemption should be scoped to the item's own label/text (or `details` should be excluded wholesale), not to `summary` alone.

samples.summary: Two bail-outs still precede the checkbox `preventDefault()`, so those paths leave a natively-flipped box disagreeing with the note
samples.evidence: The comment at 281-285 says the cancel is done "before the guards below" so no refusal path can leave the box out of step with the source. But `if (!item || !this.el.contains(item)) return;` (271) and `if (!(checkbox instanceof HTMLInputElement)) return;` (278) both run before line 286. Either firing on a click whose target *is* a real checkbox (e.g. an `input[type=checkbox]` inside a `li.task-list-item` that does not carry the `task-list-item-checkbox` class, so `item.querySelector(TASK_CHECKBOX_SELECTOR)` returns null) leaves the browser's flip in place with no document change and therefore no re-render to correct it. Not reachable through markdown-it-task-lists' fixed class today, so this is a latent gap in the invariant the comment asserts rather than a live bug.

finding.summary: replacePrefixes lets the selection map by default, so a caret at column 0 ends up BEFORE the inserted list marker
finding.evidence: `replacePrefixes` dispatches `state.update({ changes, userEvent: 'input' })` with no `selection`. CodeMirror maps the selection with assoc -1, so a cursor sitting exactly at `line.from` (the change's `from`) stays at `line.from`, i.e. in front of the `- ` / `1. ` / `- [ ] ` just written. The very same hazard is called out and fixed in the pre-existing sibling command: commands.ts:301-309 `toggleQuote` deliberately does `selection: state.selection.map(changeSet, 1)` with the comment "a caret sitting exactly at a line start would otherwise stay *before* the `> ` just inserted there, so the next keystroke would land ahead of the marker". The new code repeats the bug the old code documents. Reachable on the common paths: toggling a list on an empty line (list-commands.test.ts:96 `mount('', 0)` — the test only asserts the doc text, never the caret) or with the caret at the start of a line. The next typed character lands before the bullet and destroys the list item.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `replacePrefixes` dispatches `state.update({ changes, userEvent: 'input' })` with no `selection`, letting a caret at column 0 stay before the inserted marker. The code does not match: packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:212-219 builds `const changeSet = view.state.changes(changes)` and dispatches with `selection: view.state.selection.map(changeSet, 1)` (line 216), preceded by a comment (lines 208-211) explicitly citing the same hazard and the `toggleQuote` precedent. Grep confirms line 216 is the only selection mapping and the only other `userEvent: 'input'` in the file is in `setTaskChecked` (line 309), a length-preserving `[ ]`/`[x]` flip that carries no marker-insertion caret hazard. The two callers of `replacePrefixes` (toggleKind at line 234, shift at line 269) both funnel through that single dispatch, so no path reaches the prefix rewrite without assoc-1 mapping; on the cited `mount('', 0)` path `content === ''` so `to === from === line.from` and the caret maps past the inserted `- `. Only one list-commands.ts exists in the repo, so this is not a stale-file mixup.

finding.summary: Early returns in onTaskClick run after the browser already flipped the checkbox, without preventDefault — preview shows a checked state the source does not have
finding.evidence: `onTaskClick` returns early for `e.detail > 1` (line 271), for a nested `li` (line 282) and for `selectionTouches(item)` (line 286). All of these returns happen *before* `e.preventDefault()` (line 303). When the click landed on the `<input type="checkbox">` itself, the browser has already toggled the DOM `checked` state, and cancelling is the only thing that reverts it. On the `detail > 1` path (a user double-clicking a checkbox to tick then untick — well within the double-click interval, same position, so the second click carries `detail: 2`) the second click is ignored, nothing is written to the document, and no re-render occurs (renderPreview only runs on `docChanged`, editor.ts:421). The preview is then left displaying the opposite of what the note says, indefinitely. Fix: either `preventDefault()` before the guards when the target is the checkbox, or force a re-render.

verdict.reason: The described ordering does not exist in the repository. In packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts, `onTaskClick` computes `onCheckbox = checkbox.contains(target)` (line 279) and calls `if (onCheckbox) e.preventDefault();` at line 286 — BEFORE all subsequent guards. Furthermore the two guards the finding says would strand a flipped checkbox are explicitly disabled for checkbox clicks: line 293 is `if (!onCheckbox && e.detail > 1) return;` (so a double-click on the checkbox is processed and written via `this.onToggleTask?.(line, checked)` at line 317, not ignored) and line 302 is `if (!onCheckbox && selectionTouches(item)) return;`. The only guards after 286 that are not gated on `onCheckbox` (nested-`li` at 297-298, source-line validation at 309) run after the cancellation, so the DOM checked state is reverted anyway. The finding's cited lines (returns at 271/282/286 and preventDefault at 303) do not match the file; a repo-wide grep for `preventDefault` / `e.detail > 1` in packages/notes found no other copy of this handler.
